question: Who introduced the Iqta System in the Delhi Sultanate?
solution:
The correct answer __**Shamsuddin Iltutmish.**__

__
 
• The** Iqta System or Iqtadari System** was introduced by **Shamsuddin Iltutmish**__ of the **Delhi Sultanate. **
 
• Iqtadari System was a powerful instrument for centralization.
 
• **Iqtadari System was based **on the division of territories between Sultans and Nobility.
 
• The land was divided into small tracts and they were given to the nobles, the officers, and the soldiers. 
 
• The areas directly under Sultan came to be known as **Khalisa** and the rest of the areas were known as **Iqra.**

• Regin of Iltumish - 1211-1236 AD.
 
• Iltumish was son-in-law of Aibak.
 
• He was a Turkic slave.
 
• He was the greatest of the Slave rulers of Delhi.
 
• The Slave dynasty was established by Qutb-us-din Aibak.
 
• Dynasty lasted from 1206 to 1290.
 
• It was the first of the dynasties to rule as Sultanate in Delhi.
 
• This dynasty was succeeded by Khilji Dynasty.
